fine_trace.code:
rv = exr_attr_list_add_by_type (
            ctxt, &(curpart->attributes), name, type, 0, NULL, &nattr);
fine_trace.note: The multipart header supplies an attribute named timecode with the type string int, so the attribute list stores attacker-controlled type/name pairing.

fine_trace.code:
rv = extract_attr_32bit (
                ctxt, scratch, &(nattr->i), name, type, attrsz, 1);
fine_trace.note: Because the declared type is int, the four input bytes are parsed into the i member of the attribute union rather than into a timecode object.

Shared attribute validation only checks that both parts contain an attribute named timecode; it does not require those attributes to have type EXR_ATTR_TIMECODE before using the timecode union member.
The int values in the attribute union are reinterpreted as pointers and passed to memcmp, causing an invalid memory read during multipart shared attribute validation.
